bib.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 1280-1297

question: Can an MoE architecture be designed so each expert acquires non-overlapping, focused knowledge (expert specialization), improving quality at fixed activated compute?
hypothesis: Conventional top-K MoE (GShard) suffers knowledge hybridity and redundancy; fine-grained expert segmentation plus shared expert isolation should raise specialization and performance at equal parameters and compute.
contributions: We introduce DeepSeekMoE, an innovative MoE architecture aiming at achieving ultimate expert specialization.
We conduct extensive experiments to empirically validate the effectiveness of DeepSeekMoE and reveal its high level of expert specialization.
We scale up DeepSeekMoE to train a 16B MoE model which shows strong performance.
We will release the code and model checkpoint of DeepSeekMoE 16B to the public.

method.summary: Replaces FFNs with MoE layers using fine-grained experts (each FFN split into m smaller ones, mK activated) plus Ks always-on shared experts. Validated at ~2B params on 100B tokens against Dense, Hash Layer, Switch, GShard, then scaled to 16.4B params on 2T tokens.
method.task: MoE language model pretraining and evaluation

datasets.name: DeepSeek-AI bilingual (English/Chinese) corpus, 100B-token subset
datasets.source: corpus created by DeepSeek-AI (2024), diverse sources
datasets.preprocessing: BPE tokenizer, 8K vocab, HuggingFace Tokenizers, trained on a corpus subset

datasets.name: HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, RACE-middle, RACE-high, HumanEval, MBPP, TriviaQA, NaturalQuestions
DROP, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, WinoGrande, CLUEWSC, CEval, CMMLU, CHID (16B only)

models.name: DeepSeekMoE 2B (validation)
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer, all FFNs replaced by MoE; 1 shared + 63 routed experts, each 0.25x standard FFN, 1 shared + 7 routed activated

models.name: DeepSeekMoE 16B
models.architecture: all FFNs except first layer are MoE; 2 shared + 64 routed experts (each 0.25x FFN); token goes to 2 shared + 6 of 64 routed

models.name: Dense x16
models.architecture: 16 shared experts each standard FFN size, mimics dense model with 16x FFN params (upper bound)

training.objective: next-token prediction plus expert-level balance loss L_Bal = alpha * sum_i f_i P_i
training.lr_schedule: warmup-and-step-decay: linear 0 to max over first 2K steps, x0.316 at 80% of steps and again x0.316 at 90%
training.regularisation: gradient clipping norm 1.0; balance factor alpha 0.01 (validation), 0.001 (16B)
training.hardware: NVIDIA A100 or H800 clusters, 8 GPUs per node, NVLink (+NVSwitch on H800), InfiniBand across nodes; HAI-LLM framework with custom CUDA/Triton kernels

other.parallelism_validation: all parameters including experts on a single GPU
other.parallelism_16b: pipeline parallelism, all experts of a layer on one device
other.framework: HAI-LLM: tensor, ZeRO data, PipeDream pipeline, expert parallelism

inference.prompting: few-shot counts per benchmark: 0-shot HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC, HumanEval, WinoGrande, CHID; 5-shot RACE, TriviaQA, NQ, MMLU, CLUEWSC, CEval, CMMLU; 1-shot DROP; 8-shot GSM8K; 4-shot MATH; 3-shot MBPP

limits: Finer expert segmentation always helped, but 16B uses moderate granularity because too fine granularity lowers computational efficiency; no scaling law for granularity yet.
More activated experts may add cross-device communication overhead when experts are distributed; not measured or mitigated here.
Total expert params fixed at 16x FFN and activated at 2x FFN; optimal values at larger scale left open.
'Upper bound' claim holds only at ~2B params and 100B tokens.
16B weaker on multiple-choice tasks (MMLU, CEval, CMMLU), attributed to limited attention parameters.
No seeds, variance, throughput/latency or serving measurements; compute is reported as FLOPs only, no GPU hours.
Training corpus is proprietary; 2B validation vocab 8K differs from 16B vocab 100K.

terms.definition: existing MoE practices often employ a limited number of experts, and thus tokens assigned to a specific expert will be likely to cover diverse knowledge
tokens assigned to different experts may require common knowledge, so multiple experts converge in acquiring shared knowledge
each expert acquires non-overlapping and focused knowledge

code.snippet: h_t = sum_{i=1}^{Ks} FFN_i(u_t) + sum_{i=Ks+1}^{mN} g_{i,t} FFN_i(u_t) + u_t; g_{i,t}=s_{i,t} if s_{i,t} in Topk({s_{j,t}|Ks+1<=j<=mN}, mK-Ks) else 0; s_{i,t}=Softmax_i(u_t^T e_i)
